verdict.rationale: Vercel documents one set of primitives that scales: Fluid compute auto-scales concurrency, and the same Functions run across Hobby, Pro and Enterprise with only the limits rising (duration, memory/CPU, concurrent deployments up to 500), backed by a 99.99% Enterprise SLA. But there is no explicit commitment or evidence that apps move from prototype to massive scale without rearchitecting. Vercel KV and Vercel Postgres were also discontinued and moved to Upstash and Neon, so some storage primitives did change over time. Missing for 10: an explicit no-rearchitect or API-stability guarantee across scale, independent case evidence of apps scaling on unchanged primitives, and stable first-party data primitives.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the same core APIs and primitives from prototype through massive scale, without rearchitecting or migrating platforms as usage grows

citations.quote: Run server-side code on demand with Fluid compute, which scales concurrency for AI and I/O-heavy workloads.
Vercel is a cloud platform for building, deploying, and scaling web applications and AI workloads.
Vercel Functions run on Fluid compute, which is enabled by default for new projects.
available 99.99% of the time, excluding any Excused Downtime events
